Define a cohort by a query on a master view

Source: R/cohort_query.R
cohort_query.Rd

A definition only: nothing is read until pull_master() runs it, inside the same transaction as the pull, so the cohort and its data describe one state of the warehouse.

Usage

cohort_query(
  qualifying,
  epoch,
  index = c("first", "all"),
  prior = c("keep", "exclude")
)

Arguments

qualifying

Character. A SQL boolean expression over the master's columns, for example "proc = 'CABG'".

epoch

A Date vector of length two: first and last encounter date, inclusive.

index

"first" or "all".

prior

"keep" or "exclude", for units with a qualifying encounter before the epoch.

Value

An object of class cohort_query.

Details

The cohort is every encounter in the master that meets qualifying and falls inside epoch. index sets the study's unit: "first" keeps each patient's earliest qualifying encounter in the epoch (one row per patient; later encounters remain follow-up events), and "all" keeps every qualifying encounter in the epoch.

A patient whose qualifying encounter in the epoch was preceded by one before the epoch is a redo, not a first. Those units are always recorded as a cohort stage, prior_qualifying: prior = "keep" keeps them, prior = "exclude" drops them with a reason. Nothing is dropped silently. The earlier encounter is detected in the database; its date never leaves it.

qualifying is SQL written by the study programmer and run as a WHERE condition on the master. It must never be built from data.

See also

pull_master()

Examples

cohort_query("proc = 'CABG'", as.Date(c("2000-01-01", "2024-07-31")))
#> Cohort query: proc = 'CABG'
#>   epoch 2000-01-01 to 2024-07-31; index first; earlier qualifying encounter: keep
